newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African fuel prices set to increase - economist.
newsitem.headline: S.African fuel prices set to increase - economist.

text.p: South African gasoline and diesel prices, set monthly according to a complex formula, are likely to increase steadily in the coming months, Transnet economist Mike Schussler said on Wednesday.

Schussler predicted the price of gasoline in the Gauteng area around Johannesburg would rise to 213 cents a litre from 210 on November 6 and increase further to 218 cents in December and 222 in January, before easing back slightly.
Diesel prices were likely to rise to the same level of 213 cents next month, he added.
The average price for 1997 was likely to be around 225 for both gasoline and diesel. In 1998, he forecast diesel would cost around 235 cents and gasoline between 245 and 250.
The two key factors influencing the cost of fuel were higher international oil prices and the depreciation of the rand.
Fuel tax increases were expected in both the March 1997 and March 1998 budgets, with the tax on gasoline rising more steeply than for diesel.
